@Tarquinen Two points:

**On Rule 1 (Sticky vs last-message-only):**
You're right that there's a distinction. Our Rule 1 ("any assistant/tool → agent") differs from checking only the last message. However, this matches:
- litellm, copilot-api, crush (all use Sticky)
- VSCode's intent (tool loops, continuations, subagents all marked as `agent`)

The #8393 "last message only" approach misses synthetic user messages that OpenCode creates mid-conversation.

**On "Copilot devs confirmed":**
I searched GitHub issues, PRs, and web discussions but couldn't find this confirmation. The closest I found was @rekram1-node saying "we are working w/ copilot team to have official integration" — but no specifics about "last message only" being the correct behavior.

Could you share where this was confirmed? Happy to adjust if there's authoritative guidance I missed.

+1 for skill invocation, but I'd advocate for following the [Agent Skills open standard](https://agentskills.io/home) rather than introducing a new `/skill:<name>` syntax.

The standard (created by Anthropic) allows direct `/<skillName>` invocation - same as Claude Code and Cursor. This gives us:

- **Interoperability** - Skills work the same across Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, etc.
- **Simpler UX** - `/<skillName>` instead of `/skill:<skillName>`
- **Ecosystem alignment** - OpenCode already supports `~/.claude/skills/` paths for compatibility

Cursor's implementation: https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills
> "Skills can also be manually invoked by typing / in Agent chat and searching for the skill name"

Would love to see OpenCode follow this pattern rather than diverging with a different syntax.

I don't think this is correct assessment. This introduced the side effects of synthetic messages counting as last messages and inflating users' premium requests.

The ideal scenario would be that only messages sent by user (through CLI option or through TUI) should trigger a premium request. All subsequent messages (agent calls, tool calls, compaction) up until the agent is done their request should not trigger future requests. 

Today's logic makes too many premium request. The open PR brings us closer to a solution that should reflect appropriate behaviour.

> **Update:** Per @bowmanjd's feedback on #8067, I've refined the detection logic:
> 
> - Removed the "multiple user messages → agent" rule (was incorrect)
> - Now only checks the LAST user message for synthetic patterns
> - Real user follow-ups correctly charge premium, matching Copilot CLI behavior
> 
> See updated PR #8721 for details.
